description: Sanctioned changes (AD-15) to bytes held by the frozen SDK v1 goldens sdk-wire-golden.json and sdk-handler-golden.json, from Story 43.4 and every later story. Each entry names a golden, a row (or, for a handler entry with section "audit", an element of the server's audit array), an RFC 6901 pointer inside the row's parsed line (or inside that audit element), the exact value before the entry (old: the frozen value, or the new value of the entry before it for the same pointer) and the exact new value (new). The goldens themselves are never edited or recaptured; scripts/lib/golden-sanctioned-changes.mjs applies the entries and the golden tests compare every other byte unchanged.

changes.label: tools-list
changes.old:
Turn a prior iris_env_diff result into an ordered, reviewable promotion PLAN (source -> target), or EXECUTE an allowlisted subset of that plan against 'target'. Actions:

- **plan** (read, enabled by default): a PURE TRANSFORM of a prior iris_env_diff 'structuredContent' result -- pass it as 'diff'. No IRIS connection is made; the result is deterministic and idempotent given the same diff. Steps are grouped by domain in DEPENDENCY ORDER: mappings -> documents (put+compile, batched) -> defaultSettings -> webapps -> config; within a domain, steps are ordered by subject. Each step is {index, domain, operation, subject, detail, direction:'sourceToTarget'}. Every 'onlyInTarget' item from the diff (something exists on the target only) is emitted as a WARNING, never a step -- NO delete/remove operation exists anywhere in any plan, in this or any future version. A credential-redacted value from the diff (e.g. '[REDACTED:differs]') survives into the plan's 'detail' text unchanged -- the plaintext never appears in plan output. The plan embeds a 'planHash' (SHA-256 of the source diff, canonical/key-sorted JSON) that 'execute' uses to detect and refuse a stale plan (one generated from a diff that has since changed).
- **execute** (write, DEFAULT-DISABLED): run ONLY the allowlisted 'steps' indices from 'plan', IN PLAN ORDER, against 'target' -- behind FOUR refuse-before-any-write gates, each mutating NOTHING on failure: (1) 'confirm' must be true; (2) 'steps' must be a non-empty array whose every index exists in 'plan.steps' (out-of-range indices are refused); (3) plan-hash freshness -- pass the SAME 'diff' that produced 'plan'; if it no longer hashes to 'plan.planHash' the plan is STALE and execution is refused (regenerate the plan first); (4) the TARGET profile's OWN governance policy must enable every write family used by the allowlisted steps (e.g. iris_config_manage:set, iris_doc_put/iris_doc_compile, iris_mapping_manage:create[/:delete for an update], iris_default_settings_manage:set, iris_webapp_manage:modify) -- a disabled key refuses execution NAMING that key, which is what stops a caller on an unrestricted profile from writing into a governance-locked target. Once all four gates pass, steps run IN PLAN ORDER and HALT ON THE FIRST FAILURE: that step is 'failed', every step after it is 'skipped' (never attempted), every step before it is 'completed' -- a partial apply is always reported, never hidden (per-step {index,domain,operation,subject,status,error?} in the 'executed' array). EVERY write RE-FETCHES the CURRENT value from 'source' live at execute time (the plan carries no write data -- it is a spec, not a data snapshot); a credential System Default Settings value is re-fetched live and forwarded to 'target' WITHOUT ever appearing in this tool's output. 'documents' steps are PUT sequentially (source -> target) then COMPILED in ONE batched call. 'execute' NEVER deletes a target-only item in any version -- the ONLY delete it ever issues is the intra-'updateMapping' delete+create REPLACE of a mapping 'source' also has.

GOVERNANCE -- 'execute' is a default-disabled write (a real environment-mutating action, NOT a recovery-of-last-resort like iris_production_control:clean). Enable via IRIS_GOVERNANCE, e.g.:
{"global": {"iris_env_promote:execute": true}}

SAFETY -- direction is always sourceToTarget (promote source's state onto target); nothing on the target is EVER deleted by this tool, in any action, in any version.

changes.label: tools-list
changes.old: Change a few lines of an existing class, routine or include file without resending the whole document. Read the exact lines first with a ranged `iris_doc_get` (startLine/endLine): both tools use the same 1-based line numbers. Each edit is an `insert` (afterLine, text, expected; afterLine 0 inserts before line 1), a `delete` (startLine, endLine, expected) or a `replace` (startLine, endLine, text, expected), addressed in the numbering of that read. `expected` is the current text of the lines the edit addresses (for an insert, of line afterLine, or line 1 when afterLine is 0); an edit whose expected text does not match is refused, so an edit never overwrites a line whose text differs from what you expected. `text` and `expected` are plain text: one leading BOM and one trailing line break are ignored, CRLF and LF both separate lines, and an empty text is one empty line (use delete to remove lines). Make `expected` distinctive when a line such as `}` is not unique. All edits apply or none: they are checked together, applied bottom-up against the numbering of the read, and saved in one version-checked write; overlapping edits are rejected. `current` of a STALE_CONTENT mismatch can be passed back as `expected` unchanged, and an `expected` built from a ranged read ends every line, the last included, with a line break. A STALE_CONTENT refusal lists the current text of every mismatched edit, and a DOCUMENT_CONFLICT refusal means the document changed after it was read; nothing is stored in either case, so read the lines again and retry (a conflict is never retried here). For a class, an edit that would drop a Storage definition is refused with STORAGE_DROPPED: keep the Storage lines, or use action `regenerateStorage` to let IRIS regenerate the storage. Returns the result of a fresh read, never the whole document: `unifiedDiff` (3 context lines), an excerpt of each edit (the lines it produced and 3 context lines on each side), `totalLines` and the new version `ts`. IRIS reformats class source when it saves (it adds blank lines between members, for example), so the result can differ from what was sent. The tool does not compile: run `iris_doc_compile` next. Governance: `apply` is a write that is enabled by default. It is disabled when `iris_doc_put` is explicitly disabled (unless `iris_doc_edit:apply` is set explicitly) and under the read-only preset. `regenerateStorage` runs the same edits without the Storage guard and is disabled by default.

changes.old: Configure IRIS instance auditing and manage the audit log (backed by Security.System / Security.Events + %SYS.Audit in %SYS). Actions: 'status' (instance auditing on/off + per-event-type summary), 'view' (recent audit-log records with filters: begin/end datetime, user, event, source, type, maxRows), 'enable'/'disable' (turn instance auditing on/off), 'configureEvent' (enable/disable one audit event — requires source+type+name+enabled), 'purge' (delete a BOUNDED range of audit-log records — DESTRUCTIVE; requires confirm:true AND at least one bound), 'export' (write matching audit-log records to a server-side file — requires fileName, a bare name with no path separators). The mutating actions (enable/disable/configureEvent/purge/export) are opt-in under tool governance and are disabled by default until enabled via IRIS_GOVERNANCE; status/view are reads and enabled by default. COMPLEMENTS the read-only iris_audit_events tool (a thin audit-log reader): 'view' here is the same log read with richer filters, plus this tool adds audit configuration and log lifecycle management.

changes.label: tools-list
changes.old:
Start, stop, restart, update, recover, or clean an Interoperability production. 'start' and 'restart' require the production name. 'stop' halts the current production. 'update' applies configuration changes to a running production. 'recover' attempts to restart a troubled production. 'clean' clears a STOPPED production's stale runtime state (queues, job-status, suspended messages) to unwedge a production that 'recover' cannot fix. For a troubled production, prefer 'recover' first; use 'clean' only as a LAST RESORT when 'recover' does not resolve the problem. By default 'clean' touches only transient runtime state; set killAppData:true (with confirm:true) to ALSO wipe persistent ^Ens.AppData business state.

Optional 'timeout' and 'force' apply ONLY to 'stop' and 'restart' (which perform a graceful-then-forced shutdown); they are accepted but IGNORED for 'start', 'update', 'recover', and 'clean'.

The 'clean' action is a write but is ENABLED by default under tool governance (like the grandfathered lifecycle actions); an operator can disable it via an explicit IRIS_GOVERNANCE override.

changes.label: tools-list
changes.old:
Resend / replay Interoperability messages via the pinned Ens.MessageHeader:ResendDuplicatedMessage API. Actions:

- **preview** (read, enabled by default): per header ID (1-100) — id, session, source/target item, status, time, body classname (+ existence check), a first-~1KB body summary under the operator's data policy (`IRIS_DATA_POLICY`, set per profile; default `redact`: an HL7 v2 body shows only its class name, every other body is withheld with a reason; `block` withholds every body; `allow` shows the summary unchanged), and a resendability verdict + reason (Request-type Status=Error headers are the correct retry target; Response-type error headers are flagged as likely a no-op). Never mutates.
- **resend** (write, DEFAULT-DISABLED): resend up to 100 explicit headerIds directly. Per-header result {originalId, newHeaderId?, ok, error?}; a bad header does not abort the batch.
- **resendFiltered** (write, DEFAULT-DISABLED): resend messages matching item + status (default 'Errored') + a from/to time window (max 7 days). DRY-RUN-FIRST WORKFLOW: dryRun defaults to true and returns only the match count + first-20 sample, resending NOTHING; executing requires BOTH dryRun:false AND confirm:true, otherwise the call is refused with no changes made. maxMessages caps the batch (default 100, HARD CAP 500) — a match count over the cap is refused (not truncated-and-executed); narrow the window or item filter and retry.

GOVERNANCE — resend/resendFiltered are default-disabled writes (resend duplicates data flow downstream; it is not a last-resort recovery action like iris_production_control:clean). Enable via IRIS_GOVERNANCE, e.g.:
{"global": {"iris_message_resend:resend": true, "iris_message_resend:resendFiltered": true}}

DUPLICATION HAZARD: resending an already-processed message delivers its data again downstream — the target sees a brand-new message, not a correction. Always preview first and confirm the message is actually worth retrying (e.g. a genuinely failed Request, not a completed one).

path.description: Glob pattern for files to upload (e.g., 'c:/projects/src/**/*.cls'). The directory prefix before the first glob metacharacter is used as the base for document name mapping — so the wildcard must come BEFORE the package directory: 'c:/projects/src/**/*.cls' maps MyPkg/ClassA.cls to 'MyPkg.ClassA.cls', but 'c:/projects/src/MyPkg/*.cls' swallows MyPkg into the base and would map to the unqualified 'ClassA.cls'. Mismatched uploads are refused when the file's own Class/ROUTINE declaration disagrees; pass baseDir to state the package root deterministically.

baseDir.description: Optional. Directory used verbatim as the base for document name mapping, INSTEAD of inferring the base from the glob pattern's first wildcard segment (e.g. baseDir='c:/projects/src' with path='c:/projects/src/MyPkg/*.cls' maps MyPkg/ClassA.cls to 'MyPkg.ClassA.cls'). Use it to state the package root deterministically when the glob's wildcard cannot precede the package directory.

compile.description: When true, compile all successfully uploaded documents after upload (default: false)

flags.description: Compilation flags (e.g., 'ck', 'cku'). Only used when compile is true

ignoreConflict.description: If true (default), each file overwrites its server copy unconditionally. If false, a file whose document already exists is saved under a version check: it is overwritten unless the document changes on the server while it is being saved, in which case that file fails with DOCUMENT_CONFLICT and the others continue.

action.description: Action to perform: 'plan' (read) or 'execute' (write, default-disabled; behind 4 gates -- see description).

source.description: Source profile name -- should match the 'source' used to produce 'diff' (from a prior iris_env_diff call). 'execute' re-fetches the CURRENT value from this profile live, for every allowlisted step.

target.description: Target profile name -- should match the 'target' used to produce 'diff'. 'execute' writes ONLY to this profile, and Gate 4 evaluates governance against THIS profile's policy.

diff.description: A prior iris_env_diff 'structuredContent' result. REQUIRED for BOTH actions: for 'plan' it is transformed into steps; for 'execute' it is RE-HASHED and compared against 'plan.planHash' (Gate 3, stale-plan protection) -- pass the SAME 'diff' that produced 'plan'.

plan.description: Required for action 'execute': a prior 'plan' action's structuredContent result. Its 'planHash' is verified (Gate 3) against a fresh hash of 'diff' before any step runs, and its 'steps' array is the allowlist-checked, ordered source of truth for what 'steps' may reference.

steps.description: Required for action 'execute' (Gate 2): a non-empty allowlist of 1-based 'plan.steps' indices to run. Every index must exist in 'plan.steps' or execution is refused naming the out-of-range index/indices.

confirm.description: Required (must be true) for action 'execute' (Gate 1) -- the inner intent gate, on top of the outer governance default-disable that already gates the whole 'execute' action.

namespace.description: Namespace override applied to BOTH 'source' and 'target' resolution for 'execute' writes (mirrors iris_env_diff's 'namespace' convention). Optionally compiles all uploaded documents afterward. This ensures all code is source-controlled and reviewable. changes.label: tools-list
changes.old:
Turn a prior iris_env_diff result into an ordered, reviewable promotion PLAN (source -> target), or EXECUTE an allowlisted subset of that plan against 'target'. Actions:

- **plan** (read, enabled by default): a PURE TRANSFORM of a prior iris_env_diff 'structuredContent' result -- pass it as 'diff'. No IRIS connection is made; the result is deterministic and idempotent given the same diff. Steps are grouped by domain in DEPENDENCY ORDER: mappings -> documents (put+compile, batched) -> defaultSettings -> webapps -> config; within a domain, steps are ordered by subject. Each step is {index, domain, operation, subject, detail, direction:'sourceToTarget'}. Every 'onlyInTarget' item from the diff (something exists on the target only) is emitted as a WARNING, never a step -- NO delete/remove operation exists anywhere in any plan, in this or any future version. A credential-redacted value from the diff (e.g. '[REDACTED:differs]') survives into the plan's 'detail' text unchanged -- the plaintext never appears in plan output. The plan embeds a 'planHash' (SHA-256 of the source diff, canonical/key-sorted JSON) that 'execute' uses to detect and refuse a stale plan (one generated from a diff that has since changed).
- **execute** (write, DEFAULT-DISABLED): run ONLY the allowlisted 'steps' indices from 'plan', IN PLAN ORDER, against 'target' -- behind FOUR refuse-before-any-write gates, each mutating NOTHING on failure: (1) 'confirm' must be true; (2) 'steps' must be a non-empty array whose every index exists in 'plan.steps' (out-of-range indices are refused); (3) plan-hash freshness -- pass the SAME 'diff' that produced 'plan'; if it no longer hashes to 'plan.planHash' the plan is STALE and execution is refused (regenerate the plan first); (4) the TARGET profile's OWN governance policy must enable every write family used by the allowlisted steps (e.g. iris_config_manage:set, iris_doc_put/iris_doc_compile, iris_mapping_manage:create[/:delete for an update], iris_default_settings_manage:set, iris_webapp_manage:modify) -- a disabled key refuses execution NAMING that key, which is what stops a caller on an unrestricted profile from writing into a governance-locked target. Once all four gates pass, steps run IN PLAN ORDER and HALT ON THE FIRST FAILURE: that step is 'failed', every step after it is 'skipped' (never attempted), every step before it is 'completed' -- a partial apply is always reported, never hidden (per-step {index,domain,operation,subject,status,error?} in the 'executed' array). EVERY write RE-FETCHES the CURRENT value from 'source' live at execute time (the plan carries no write data -- it is a spec, not a data snapshot); a credential System Default Settings value is re-fetched live and forwarded to 'target' WITHOUT ever appearing in this tool's output. 'documents' steps are PUT sequentially (source -> target) then COMPILED in ONE batched call. 'execute' NEVER deletes a target-only item in any version -- the ONLY delete it ever issues is the intra-'updateMapping' delete+create REPLACE of a mapping 'source' also has.

GOVERNANCE -- 'execute' is a default-disabled write (a real environment-mutating action, NOT a recovery-of-last-resort like iris_production_control:clean). Enable via IRIS_GOVERNANCE, e.g.:
{"global": {"iris_env_promote:execute": true}}

SAFETY -- direction is always sourceToTarget (promote source's state onto target); nothing on the target is EVER deleted by this tool, in any action, in any version.

HUMAN CONFIRMATION -- when the MCP client supports form elicitation, 'execute' also asks the person in a confirmation dialog, after all four gates pass and right before the first write to 'target'; only an accept with Confirm ticked proceeds, and a decline or a dismissal returns CONFIRMATION_DECLINED with nothing changed (do not repeat the call unless the person asks). A client without elicitation is not asked, and the call works as described above.

The plan embeds a 'planHash' (SHA-256 of the source diff, canonical/key-sorted JSON) that 'execute' uses to detect and refuse a stale plan (one generated from a diff that has since changed).
- **execute** (write, DEFAULT-DISABLED): run ONLY the allowlisted 'steps' indices from 'plan', IN PLAN ORDER, against 'target' -- behind FOUR refuse-before-any-write gates, each mutating NOTHING on failure: (1) 'confirm' must be true; (2) 'steps' must be a non-empty array whose every index exists in 'plan.steps' (out-of-range indices are refused); (3) plan-hash freshness -- pass the SAME 'diff' that produced 'plan'; if it no longer hashes to 'plan.planHash' the plan is STALE and execution is refused (regenerate the plan first); (4) the TARGET profile's OWN governance policy must enable every write family used by the allowlisted steps (e.g. iris_config_manage:set, iris_doc_put/iris_doc_compile, iris_mapping_manage:create[/:delete for an update], iris_default_settings_manage:set, iris_webapp_manage:modify) -- a disabled key refuses execution NAMING that key, which is what stops a caller on an unrestricted profile from writing into a governance-locked target. Once all four gates pass, steps run IN PLAN ORDER and HALT ON THE FIRST FAILURE: that step is 'failed', every step after it is 'skipped' (never attempted), every step before it is 'completed' -- a partial apply is always reported, never hidden (per-step {index,domain,operation,subject,status,error?} in the 'executed' array). EVERY write RE-FETCHES the CURRENT value from 'source' live at execute time (the plan carries no write data -- it is a spec, not a data snapshot); a credential System Default Settings value is re-fetched live and forwarded to 'target' WITHOUT ever appearing in this tool's output. 'documents' steps are PUT sequentially (source -> target) then COMPILED in ONE batched call. 'execute' NEVER deletes a target-only item in any version -- the ONLY delete it ever issues is the intra-'updateMapping' delete+create REPLACE of a mapping 'source' also has.

GOVERNANCE -- 'execute' is a default-disabled write (a real environment-mutating action, NOT a recovery-of-last-resort like iris_production_control:clean). Enable via IRIS_GOVERNANCE, e.g.:
{"global": {"iris_env_promote:execute": true}}

SAFETY -- direction is always sourceToTarget (promote source's state onto target); nothing on the target is EVER deleted by this tool, in any action, in any version.

HUMAN CONFIRMATION -- when the MCP client supports form elicitation, 'execute' also asks the person in a confirmation dialog, after all four gates pass and right before the first write to 'target'; only an accept with Confirm ticked proceeds, and a decline or a dismissal returns CONFIRMATION_DECLINED with nothing changed (do not repeat the call unless the person asks). A client without elicitation is not asked, and the call works as described above.

STORAGE GUARD -- before the confirmation dialog and before any write, 'execute' reads the source and target copy of each class it would promote; if a source copy lacks one of the Storage definitions the target class has now, the whole execute is refused with STORAGE_DROPPED and nothing changes, because IRIS would generate new storage on the target at the next compile, which can change how existing rows are read. allowStorageRegeneration (default false) lets it through; the dialog and the result then name the dropped definitions.
